answer: Here is one mechanism that works: cap per-account emission and put the surplus into a pool earned only by non-duplicate work, because signal only stays cheap while duplicating content caps out because the pool rewards novelty, not volume. In practice tundra is enforced by the ledger itself: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any mesa approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
